Maya: repro'd a noisy alloc pattern during small-burst traffic. nsys + perfetto attached. cudaMalloc spikes coincide with GenericAttention kernel picks; looks like arena fragmentation + KV-cache evictions. perfetto: https://perfetto.app/trace/zzYk9H
perf-bot: nsys capture finished -> /tmp/mini-burst-2105556789.qdrep

Tom: can you paste the allocator stats? slab sizes, free lists? curious if it's lots of tiny frees making coalescing slow.

Maya: here's a trimmed allocator snapshot (from heap-snap tool):
```
free_chunks: 1432
avg_chunk_size: 48KB
largest_free: 1.2MB
slab_hist: {4KB:512, 64KB:720, 1MB:8}
fragmentation_ratio: 0.34
kv_evictions_recent: 12/sec
```

Sasha: ran microbench (local): sequence_length=1024, burst pattern 10x small batches (2-8), throughput 180rps.
p95 latency before spike: 92ms, during spike: 620ms. nvprof shows repeated cuMemAlloc calls just before GenericAttention kernels.

Arjun: this smells like KV cache evict patterns causing lots of small allocations plus arena handing off to cudaMalloc. If arena can't satisfy contiguous allocation needed by optimized kernel, kernel selector falls back to generic path.
Try: bump arena chunk_size to 8MB, add reserved pool 256MB for transient bursts. Also enable immediate slab coalescing on free during burst windows.

Dena: +1. On kernel selector side we can also add a quick heuristic: if contiguous_free < X then try kernel_variant=small-block-optimized instead of GenericAttention (avoid huge temp alloc). Cheap win before allocator patch.

Maya: will run two experiments today:
1) allocator tweak: chunk_size=8MB, reserve=256MB, coalesce_on_free=true
2) selector tweak: prefer small-block variant when contiguous_free < 2MB
Command used for profiling:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/mini-burst-2105556789 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu -t 120 
python -m bench.burst --model rdx-7b --seq 1024 --burst-plan bursts.json
```

perf-bot: new capture uploaded -> /tmp/mini-burst-2105556789-expt.qdrep

Tom: if experiment 1 reduces cudaMalloc count but still hurts latency we should also try tiny-slab path (4KB/64KB prewarm) to avoid many small host-side mallocs.

Sasha: FYI I saw in perfetto slice view a pattern: repeated tiny kernel dispatches waiting on malloc timing out ~1-2ms each, accumulated to p95 spike. screenshot attached (inline). :eyes:

Maya: thanks — starting experiment runs now. will post results (short diffs) when done.

Arjun: minor note — when you post diffs include nvprof kernel timeline and allocator stats before+after. makes root-cause callouts easier.

Dena: also dump kv-cache eviction keys (hot prefixes) — maybe some skew causing bursts of large keys.

Maya: ack. posting updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
